title: Staged A/B Orchestrator with Atomic Commit and Fallback Hooks
author: Aisha Khatri
description:
Context: Customers require a single control-plane primitive to run multi-arm A/B tests and staged feature rollouts while guaranteeing either instantaneous or safe rollback semantics. Existing controllers occasionally left the system in an inconsistent state when a control-plane failure occurred mid-rollout (traffic split applied but assignment metadata missing), or when deterministic canaries needed to be committed atomically across the routing plane and feature flags.

What this PR does: Implements a Staged A/B Orchestrator that supports: 1) atomic commit semantics for model swaps and traffic assignments (two-phase commit with short-lived leases); 2) schedule-aware windows and blackout periods to prevent rollouts during known maintenance windows; 3) preflight validators and lightweight shadow replays as fallback hooks; 4) a rollback oracle that performs targeted snapshot replays against a representative cohort and votes on a rollback if SLOs regress beyond configured thresholds; 5) an audit-friendly journaling layer to replay and reconcile partially-applied rollouts.

Design highlights: The orchestrator separates plan and apply phases. A plan describes cohorts, routing weights, validation probes, and a commit deadline. Apply uses a lease-based coordinator that first attempts a control-plane prepare step (allocating ephemeral assignment keys), then issues phased routing changes to edge proxies with a fast path for single-step atomic swaps (when config allows). If any validator fails, the apply either triggers a rollback hook or pauses and marks the plan as quarantined for manual inspection.

Safety gates and metrics: Validators include latency delta, error-rate delta, schema-conformance for structured outputs, token-level perplexity regressions (for generated text), and a sampling-based equality test between primary/shadow outputs for deterministic models. The rollback oracle aggregates weighted signals and includes hysteresis to avoid flapping. All actions are emitted to tracing and an audit journal for later replay.

Why unique: Unlike prior rollout controllers, this implementation focuses on atomic semantics across the control and data planes rather than optimistic, eventually-consistent handoffs. It also integrates lightweight shadow replay and a configurable rollback oracle as first-class primitives.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added for the prepare/apply/commit phases, and an end-to-end chaos test that kills the coordinator mid-apply to validate the reconciliation/journal path. Feature rollout plan will be gated behind a feature flag and enabled for internal tenants first, then open to customers after a one-week canary.

Notes: This PR touches control-plane reconciliation, routing proxies, and the telemetry schema. Backwards compatibility kept by exposing the new API under /v2/rollouts and keeping v1 behavior intact.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-3872; [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests; [x] chaos tests; [x] docs stub in repo; [x] telemetry and alerts updated.

Related: builds on previous work in ENG-3410 (cohort rollouts) and PM-114 (experiment lifecycle).

review_comments: Miguel Santos (reviewer): Nice end-to-end testing. Two requests: 1) can we reduce the default commit lease TTL to 12s? 2) add a unit test covering validator timeouts.
Aisha Khatri (author): Reduced commit lease TTL to 12s and added validator timeout test in validators/tests/test_timeouts.py. Updated doc to explain tradeoffs.

Priya Raman (reviewer): The perplexity probe looks good but we should not use absolute token-level thresholds across models. Suggest model-scoped baselining and a per-model historical z-score threshold.
Aisha Khatri (author): Switched to z-score based thresholds stored in model profiles; added implementation and tests. Also added a note in docs about baselining data retention.
Jonah Lee (reviewer): Can we ensure that partial apply leaves a deterministic journal entry so reconciliation is idempotent? Also flagged a minor race in the lease renewal path.

Aisha Khatri (author): Journal entries are now strictly append-only with explicit prepare/commit markers; fixed race in lease renewal by serializing renewals on the lease object. Added comment and test.

release_notes: Introduces v2 rollout API with atomic commit semantics, schedule-aware A/B scheduling, preflight validators, shadow replay fallback, and a rollback oracle. Feature gated; no user-facing breaking changes. See docs/rollouts/v2.md for usage.
notes_for_ops: Monitor rollout.events.* metrics and set alert for 'rollback_oracle.votes' > 5 within 10m. Keep the feature flag off for critical customers until internal canary completes.
